description:
Twelve near-black tiles, each holding one centred, radially symmetric rosette that floats in the middle of the frame and never touches an edge. Flat vector shapes only: no gradients, no texture, no line work except the drawn marks themselves; the soft passages are all produced by translucent shapes overlapping each other. Three material families recur in every seed. First, the body: a mass of overlapping rectangular slabs and tapered wedges fanned out from the centre in a ring, in ochre/mustard gold, with the ones underneath reading darker olive-umber where they are shaded or overlapped. The slabs give the disc a ragged, stepped, sawtooth silhouette rather than a clean circle. Second, an interior mark set in cool slate blue-grey: depending on seed it is fat petals (9011, 10085), comma or crescent hooks arranged in rings (9548, 10622), branching dendritic whiskers (10801), or thin feathery filaments swept into a spiral pinwheel (9369). Third, a rim population of small dark appendages: hooks, crescents, teeth and, in some seeds, long thin curling hairs or tendrils that reach well outside the disc (9727, 9906, 10264). The overall read is biological and specimen-like: a sunflower head, a sea urchin, an anemone, a thistle, a pollen grain, a pressed and mounted radiolarian. It does not read as architecture, machinery, or landscape.

The palette is three hues and no more, and it is the same three in all twelve: ochre gold as the dominant mass, slate blue-grey as the only cool accent, dark olive-brown for the shaded understructure, all on a flat near-black ground that is also the sheet background, so the tiles have no visible border and the objects appear to hang in the same continuous dark. Contrast is carried almost entirely by gold-against-black at the silhouette and by slate-against-gold inside; there is no third contrast register.

What the twelve share: same centring, same scale envelope (roughly 55-70 percent of the tile), same circular overall footprint, same radial symmetry of about 6 to 12 repeats, same three materials, same palette. What separates them is essentially density and which mark family dominates. 9011 and 10085 are the highest contrast, reading as flowers with slate petals against a gold ground; 10085 is the darkest and most graphic, almost a heraldic star. 9548, 10264 and 10622 are gold discs packed with slate commas. 10801 is the largest and fuzziest, a wide gold pad with slate branching strokes. 9369 is the most empty: a nearly plain gold disc with one small spiral of pale filaments in the centre and a lot of unmarked field. 9190, 9906, 10443 and 10980 have almost no slate at all and read as plain gold spiky bursts; 10443 is the weakest and thinnest of the set, small, dark and scraggly. Several seeds have appendages that appear fully detached from the body and float alone in the black (9011 far left, 9906 lower left, 10264 upper right), which reads either as shed spores or as debris depending on how charitable you are.

Across the three market states the change is large, systematic, and mostly one of scale and brightness. Stress is the biggest and brightest state in every seed shown: the wedges lengthen and multiply, the disc expands to nearly fill the tile, and the gold lifts to a lighter, more saturated value (9369 goes from a modest disc to a broad full sunburst; 9011 grows a dense second ring of long spokes; 9548 swells and its commas enlarge). Neutral is the smallest, darkest and most contained. Recovery sits between the two in size, but is distinguished by more than scale: its interior marks are rotated and swept into a swirl, so 9011 recovery has a pinwheel core where 9011 neutral has a symmetric petal ring, and 9369 recovery has a larger, more elaborate, visibly twisted filament spiral. So the direction of the change is that stress makes the specimen bloom and brighten and expand, and neutral is the quiet contracted state.

At 120px everything essential survives: the silhouette, the gold-on-black read, the rim fringe, the presence or absence of a slate core, and the state change (a stress tile is obviously bigger and paler than its neutral tile at thumbnail size, and same-seed identity holds across all three states). What does not fully survive at 120 is the distinction between the twelve. The interior mark families collapse into about three or four recognisable kinds: slate-cored flower (9011, 9727, 10085), gold disc with a slate speckle field (9369, 9548, 10264, 10622, 10801), and plain gold spiky burst with an empty middle (9190, 9906, 10443, 10980). Within those groups the seeds are hard to tell apart at browse size, particularly 9190 against 9906 and 10980, which read as one stamp at three rotations.
